Co-author: @tomasruizt 
Based on https://github.com/tomasruizt/vllm/pull/18

## Overview

Fixes output distribution shift under spec decode + structured outputs: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60451

Architecture overview at https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/62818.

Alternative to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60690.

## Claims

Fixes the issue with minor performance gains on the async scheduling path (~2%) and a ~2% regression on the sync path.

## Validation

Correctness:

Most direct validation is `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_distribution_shift.py`, which mirrors the issue's setup.
- Sample 4000 samples with the same prompt and regex grammar but with spec decode on vs off
- Compare the sampled distributions
- Distributions differ significantly on main but don't on this branch

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py   \
       tests/v1/structured_output   \
       tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_invalid_drafts.py

501 passed, 2 xfailed, 56 warnings in 237.92s (0:03:57)

pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_distribution_shift.py   \
       tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dflash/   \
       -k "not dflash2"

9 passed, 1 deselected, 19 warnings in 996.13s (0:16:36)
```

Performance:

https://gist.github.com/yzong-rh/e550d5fb57af73372f57dc0c7c5e694b

`Qwen/Qwen3-4B` + `RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-speculator.dspark` + 15 draft tokens + adaptive verification
Run on 1 H100 80GB

```
.venv/bin/python run.py --output ./bench_res/... --num-repeats 10
```

Results report throughput in tokens/s.
- sync vs async scheduling
- broad vs tight constraints: less vocab masked vs more vocab masked
- c1 vs c96: low vs high concurrency
- brackets report 95% confidence intervals

| Case | main | #60690 | this |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| sync / broad / c1 | 536.0 [518.8, 553.2] | 526.1 [510.7, 541.6] -1.85% | 524.8 [513.4, 536.2] -2.09% |
| sync / broad / c96 | 10,375.9 [10,349.6, 10,402.1] | 10,161.8 [10,125.0, 10,198.6] -2.06% | 10,176.5 [10,149.4, 10,203.6] -1.92% |
| sync / tight / c1 | 856.9 [823.4, 890.4] | 858.6 [847.6, 869.6] +0.20% | 857.3 [837.8, 876.7] +0.04% |
| sync / tight / c96 | 17,539.1 [17,483.4, 17,594.7] | 17,089.6 [17,026.4, 17,152.9] -2.56% | 17,062.5 [17,007.0, 17,118.0] -2.72% |
| async / broad / c1 | 669.0 [667.4, 670.6] | 663.5 [662.0, 665.0] -0.83% | 666.9 [664.8, 668.9] -0.32% |
| async / broad / c96 | 10,017.3 [10,003.0, 10,031.5] | 9,969.8 [9,908.9, 10,030.7] -0.47% | 10,358.9 [10,340.3, 10,377.5] +3.41% |
| async / tight / c1 | 1,081.6 [1,077.5, 1,085.6] | 1,082.8 [1,077.4, 1,088.2] +0.12% | 1,078.3 [1,077.3, 1,079.2] -0.31% |
| async / tight / c96 | 17,066.4 [17,020.3, 17,112.5] | 16,862.1 [16,622.7, 17,101.6] -1.20% | 17,462.7 [17,411.0, 17,514.5] +2.32% |

## Details

`StructuredOutputManager` changes (`vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py`)
- Rename `validate_tokens` to `trim_spec_tokens`; no longer trim the rejected invalid token
- Allow `grammar_bitmask` to handle unvalidated draft tokens; previously, all draft tokens were already validated by `validate_tokens`

Scheduling changes (`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`):
- Remove the `StructuredOutputManager.validate_tokens` call on the async scheduling path

`StructuredOutputGrammar` changes:
- Ensure `StructuredOutputGrammar.accept_tokens` is atomic on failure: when it returns False (acceptance fails), grammar state is not updated
- Allow `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask` to call `StructuredOutputGrammar.accept_tokens` with unvalidated draft tokens, without an extra `StructuredOutputManager.validate_tokens` call
- Update to XGrammar backend to rollback accepted tokens when `StructuredOutputGrammar.accept_tokens` fails
- Update to Guidance backend to use `ll_matcher.try_consume_tokens` + rollback vs `ll_matcher.consume_tokens` to not advance matcher state when `StructuredOutputGrammar.accept_tokens` fails

`EngineCore` changes:
- Comment update only

</details>

nodes.body: I think we should include `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/distribution_shift.py` in the tests, because it catches the issue from the client side

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @yzong-rh.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

Added `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_distribution_shift.py`, still seeing ~4% regression on sync high concurrency cases. Parity on async cases. Will compare against https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60690

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @yzong-rh.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

Independently checked `3b0d447c` on Linux/Python 3.12 with Torch `2.14.0+cpu`, XGrammar `0.2.8`, llguidance `1.7.6` and outlines_core `0.2.14`:

- Your unchanged backend test on parent `4bd75e95`: **1 failed, 2 passed, 1 xfailed**. XGrammar rejects the subsequent `[first]` after the failed `[first, invalid]`, reproducing the state leak.
- The same test on this head: **3 passed, 1 xfailed**.
- The complete `test_structured_output_manager.py` on this head: **66 passed, 1 xfailed**.

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/structured_output/test_grammar_backends.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py
```

These used raw Git source snapshots with existing CPU dependencies and pinned local GPT-2/config metadata; only the new backend test was overlaid on the parent. No production changes. Existing xfails and deprecation/source-version warnings remain. No model weights, GPU, sampling-distribution E2E or performance validation. Codex-assisted verification.

✅ @yzong-rh, CI is now available for this PR.

- `/ci run` starts upstream CI; `/amd-ci run` starts AMD CI only.

- `/ci retry` retries failed jobs in the CI build for the current PR head. If the current head has no CI build, it starts a new CI build for the current head containing only jobs that failed in the latest earlier CI build for this PR.
- `/amd-ci retry` retries failed jobs in AMD CI for the current PR head. Use `/amd-ci run` when the current head has no AMD CI build.
- `/ci cancel` cancels scheduled or running CI builds for this PR branch; `/amd-ci cancel` does the same for AMD CI only.

<!-- vllm-ci-authorized -->

Failing tests asserted that acceptance rate under a sync scheduling baseline matches acceptance rate under async scheduling. This is no longer true as async scheduling no longer trims grammar-invalid draft tokens.

The actual # of drafts proposed, verified, or accepted haven't changed, only the reported metrics ("vllm:spec_decode_num_draft_tokens") changed for async scheduling. Said metrics are being made more consistent in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/64099.

For now, I updated the tests to assert on acceptance lengths, which is more consistent, instead of acceptance rate

```
pytest -v -s \
  tests/v1/e2e/general/test_async_scheduling.py::test_with_eagle3_spec_decoding \
  tests/v1/e2e/general/test_async_scheduling.py::test_with_ngram_gpu_spec_decoding \
  tests/v1/e2e/general/test_async_scheduling_accuracy.py::test_with_eagle3_spec_decoding \
  tests/v1/e2e/general/test_async_scheduling_accuracy.py::test_with_ngram_gpu_spec_decoding
```

Pass on 1xH100

Also re-ran listed validation in the description. Still pass

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

I didn't get into the all details of spec decoding + structured output yet, but for me this PR looks good to fix the reported issue https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/62818. Do not want to slow things down for now, the general idea of fixing the problem is clear for me.
LGTM

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+from collections import Counter
+
+import pytest
+import regex as re
+from scipy.stats import chi2_contingency
+
+from tests.utils import single_gpu_only
+from vllm import SamplingParams
+from vllm.sampling_params import StructuredOutputsParams
+
+from .utils import compute_acceptance_rate
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rejection_sample_method", ["standard", "block"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("async_scheduling", [False, True], ids=["sync", "async"])
+@single_gpu_only
+def test_structured_output_preserves_sampling_distribution(
+    rejection_sample_method, async_scheduling, vllm_runner
+):
+    spec_config = {
+        "method": "dflash",
+        "model": "z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16",
+        "num_speculative_tokens": 3,
+        "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic",
+        "rejection_sample_method": rejection_sample_method,
+    }
+    regex = r'\{"city": "(Paris|Berlin|Madrid)"\}'
+    num_samples = 4000
+    cities_counts = []
+    for config in (None, spec_config):
+        with vllm_runner(
+            "Qwen/Qwen3-4B",
+            speculative_config=config,
+            async_scheduling=async_scheduling,
+            enforce_eager=True,
+            enable_prefix_caching=False,
+            gpu_memory_utilization=0.8,
+            disable_log_stats=False,
+        ) as runner:
+            params = [
+                SamplingParams(
+                    temperature=1.0,
+                    max_tokens=32,
+                    seed=i,
+                    structured_outputs=StructuredOutputsParams(regex=regex),
+                )
+                for i in range(num_samples)
+            ]
+            outputs = runner.get_llm().chat(
+                [[{"role": "user", "content": "Name a random European capital."}]]
+                * num_samples,
+                params,
+                use_tqdm=False,
+                chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": False},
+            )
+            if config is not None:
+                assert compute_acceptance_rate(runner.get_llm().get_metrics()) > 0
+            texts = [o.outputs[0].text for o in outputs]
+            assert all(re.fullmatch(regex, text) for text in texts), (
+                "Grammar-invalid output"
+            )
+            cities_counts.append(Counter(texts))
+    assert_grammar_distribution_unchanged(*cities_counts)
+
+
+def assert_grammar_distribution_unchanged(counts1: Counter[str], counts2: Counter[str]):
+    outcomes = sorted(counts1.keys() | counts2.keys())
+    row1 = [counts1[outcome] for outcome in outcomes]
+    row2 = [counts2[outcome] for outcome in outcomes]
+    _, p, _, _ = chi2_contingency([row1, row2], correction=False)
+    assert p > 1e-3, (
+        f"Grammar output distributions differ: {counts1=}, {counts2=}, {p=}"
+    )
